title: Addition and subtraction of linear expressions
summary: Add and subtract linear expressions by removing brackets correctly and combining only terms with identical variable parts.
objectives: Identify like terms by matching their complete variable parts.
Add and subtract expressions while preserving every sign.
Verify equivalent expressions through substitution or reverse grouping.

blocks.text: Like terms have exactly the same variable part, including every variable and exponent. The terms 4x and −7x are like terms, while 4x and 4x² are not. Constants form their own group. Combine coefficients and keep the shared variable part unchanged.

Addition allows brackets to be removed without changing internal signs. Subtraction is different: subtracting an expression means adding its opposite, so every sign in the subtracted bracket changes. Writing an intermediate line prevents the minus sign from affecting only the first term.

blocks.text: Expressions may contain several variables. Treat x-terms, y-terms and constants as separate columns. A term xy belongs to another group because its variable part contains both x and y. Reordering by the commutative law makes the groups visible without changing their values.

Keep the sign attached to each term while moving it. The expression above simplifies to 2x + 2y − 2. A negative coefficient belongs to the term, so −2y must move as one unit rather than leaving its minus sign behind.

sections.title: Use substitution to detect sign errors

blocks.text: Two expressions are equivalent when they have the same value for every permitted variable choice. Substituting one convenient set of values is a useful error check, although it is not a proof. Values such as 0, 1 and −1 expose missing constants and sign changes quickly.

Common errors include combining unlike terms, changing only the first sign after a subtraction bracket, or losing a zero coefficient. If x-terms cancel, write 0x mentally and retain any remaining y-terms and constants. Then present the final expression without the zero term.

blocks.text: Attach each sign to its term, remove addition brackets directly, and change every sign in a subtracted bracket. Group terms only when their full variable parts match, combine their coefficients, and keep constants separate. Check the simplified form with a simple substitution.
